page: Hetzner Cloud cax21 is a shared-core virtual server provisioned within the provider's Cost Optimized family via the QEMU hypervisor. The instance is powered by an arm64 Ampere Altra processor based on the Neoverse-N1 microarchitecture, clocked at 2.0 GHz. It is configured with 4 shared virtual CPUs across 4 physical cores with one thread per core, paired with 8.0 GB of memory (1.95 GB per core). For persistent local storage, the instance includes an 80 GB NVMe SSD. Hardware accelerators such as GPUs are not present, and the configuration does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results demonstrate consistent mid-tier execution in standard system compute tests, offset by lower throughput in highly parallelized or specialized instructions. Synthetic CPU evaluations via stress-ng yield average results in both single-core (1777.99) and multi-core (7055.54) execution tiers. However, in Geekbench testing, the single-core score of 1005.0 and multi-core score of 3335.0 place the instance in the lower quartile, reflecting the modest 2.0 GHz clock speed and Neoverse-N1 architecture. Extended instruction tests, such as PassMark encryption (637.38) and Geekbench image processing (1893.0), exhibit bottom-decile relative performance due to the lack of AVX or specialized x86 vector instruction sets, though hardware AES cryptography is available.

Memory bandwidth measurements highlight a 275.77 GB/sec cached small-block throughput and moderate uncached large-block capabilities, reaching 45.11 GB/sec read and 26.08 GB/sec write. Workload-specific operations show steady performance for PassMark database tasks (2684.51), while in-memory throughput achieves 4.44 million operations per second on Redis SET benchmarks. Web delivery delivers 4.52 GB/sec in static web serving benchmarks. Micro-model language inference tests on a 135M model show prompt ingestion at 169.73 tokens per second and token generation at 46.26 tokens per second.

Given its arm64 architecture, shared allocation, and 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio, Hetzner Cloud cax21 operates as a cost-efficient platform for horizontal application deployments. It is suited for lightweight microservices, testing environments, staging servers, edge web proxies, and CI/CD tasks built for 64-bit ARM architectures.
description: Hetzner Cloud cax21 is an arm64 cloud instance configured with 4 shared vCPUs on an Ampere Altra Neoverse-N1 processor operating at 2.0 GHz. The virtual machine includes 8.0 GB of RAM (1.95 GB per vCPU) and a local 80 GB NVMe SSD, managed via the QEMU hypervisor without GPU acceleration. In benchmark evaluations, the cax21 displays middle-tier stress-ng multi-core and database operational throughput, though raw single-thread scores and vector computation benchmarks place it in lower percentiles. With 45.11 GB/sec uncached memory read bandwidth and solid basic cryptographic processing through hardware AES, the server offers high resource density on shared hardware. It represents an economical option tailored for lightweight web serving, testing environments, background utility scripts, and native ARM CI/CD compilation workloads.
